title: Splitting of an injection measured on a free presentation of the cokernel
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $u:N\to M$ an injective homomorphism of $R$-modules, $Q=M/u(N)$ with projection $p:M\to Q$, and $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ an exact sequence of $R$-modules with $F_0$ free. Let $\alpha:F_0\to M$ be an $R$-linear map with $p\circ\alpha=\pi$, and let $\beta:F_1\to N$ be the unique $R$-linear map with $u\circ\beta=\alpha\circ d_1$ (it exists since $p\circ\alpha\circ d_1=\pi\circ d_1=0$, so $\alpha\circ d_1$ takes values in $u(N)$, and it is unique since $u$ is injective). Then $u$ has an $R$-linear left inverse $v:M\to N$ ($v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$) if and only if there is an $R$-linear map $\gamma:F_0\to N$ with $\beta=\gamma\circ d_1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion, lemma at line 18142, proof from line 18151, the sentence at lines 18166-18168): 'The extension above is split if and only if there exists a map gamma : F_0 -> N such that beta = gamma o d_1', stated there without proof

proof.text: *($\Rightarrow$).* Let $v:M\to N$ be $R$-linear with $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$ and put $\gamma=v\circ\alpha:F_0\to N$, an $R$-linear map. Then $\gamma\circ d_1=v\circ\alpha\circ d_1=v\circ u\circ\beta=\beta$, using $u\circ\beta=\alpha\circ d_1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion, proof at lines 18151 ff., the sentence at lines 18166-18168), the sentence 'The extension above is split if and only if there exists a map gamma : F_0 -> N such that beta = gamma o d_1', asserted there without proof; the argument is written out here

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$), set-up: $M=u(N)+\alpha(F_0)$.* Let $\gamma:F_0\to N$ be $R$-linear with $\gamma\circ d_1=\beta$. Define the $R$-linear maps $\Phi:N\oplus F_0\to M$, $\Phi(n,x)=u(n)+\alpha(x)$, and $\Psi:N\oplus F_0\to N$, $\Psi(n,x)=n+\gamma(x)$. $\Phi$ is surjective: given $m\in M$, exactness of $F_1\to F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ at $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] says $\pi$ is surjective, so there is $x\in F_0$ with $\pi(x)=p(m)$; then $p(m-\alpha(x))=p(m)-\pi(x)=0$, so $m-\alpha(x)\in\ker p=u(N)$ ($Q=M/u(N)$), say $m-\alpha(x)=u(n)$, and $m=\Phi(n,x)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion, proof at lines 18151 ff., the sentence at lines 18166-18168), the sentence 'The extension above is split if and only if there exists a map gamma : F_0 -> N such that beta = gamma o d_1', asserted there without proof; the argument is written out here

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$), $\ker\Phi\subseteq\ker\Psi$.* Let $(n,x)\in N\oplus F_0$ with $u(n)+\alpha(x)=0$. Applying $p$ gives $\pi(x)=p(\alpha(x))=-p(u(n))=0$, so $x\in\ker\pi$, and by exactness of $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q$ at $F_0$ ($\ker\pi=\operatorname{Im}d_1$) [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] there is $y\in F_1$ with $x=d_1(y)$. Then $u(n)=-\alpha(d_1(y))=-u(\beta(y))$, so $n=-\beta(y)$ because $u$ is injective. Hence $\Psi(n,x)=n+\gamma(d_1(y))=-\beta(y)+\beta(y)=0$, using $\gamma\circ d_1=\beta$.

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$), the left inverse.* By step 2, $\Phi$ induces an $R$-linear isomorphism $(N\oplus F_0)/\ker\Phi\cong M$, and by step 3, $\Psi$ factors through the quotient $(N\oplus F_0)/\ker\Phi$ (homomorphism theorem for modules). So there is a unique $R$-linear $v:M\to N$ with $v\circ\Phi=\Psi$, explicitly $v(u(n)+\alpha(x))=n+\gamma(x)$. For $n\in N$: $v(u(n))=v(\Phi(n,0))=\Psi(n,0)=n$, i.e. $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$, so $u$ has an $R$-linear left inverse. (Neither direction uses that $F_0$ is free; freeness is what guarantees that a lift $\alpha$ exists, and $\alpha$ is given in the statement.)
